ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached Lewis structure shows sulfur, S, in the center. Four oxygen atoms, O, are bonded to the central sulfur: one above, one below, one to the left, and one to the right. The oxygen atoms have lone-pair dots drawn around them, and no lone pairs are indicated on the central sulfur. Reasoning: Around sulfur there are four S–O bonding regions. Each single bond counts as one electron domain, so sulfur has 4 electron domains total and 0 lone-pair domains indicated. By VSEPR theory, an AX4 arrangement has a tetrahedral molecular geometry. Therefore, the geometric shape is tetrahedral.
